## Life, Death, Resurrection, and Judgment {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="120"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p120" title="Paragraph 120 in the full text">120</a></div><div class="note-text">Consider how with this one verse which hath descended from the heaven of the Will of God, the world and all that is therein have been brought to a reckoning with Him. Whosoever acknowledged His truth and turned unto Him, his good works outweighed his misdeeds, and all his sins were remitted and forgiven. Thereby is the truth of these words concerning Him made manifest: “Swift is He in reckoning.” Thus God turneth iniquity into righteousness, were ye to explore the realms of divine knowledge, and fathom the mysteries of His wisdom. In like manner, whosoever partook of the cup of love, obtained his portion of the ocean of eternal grace and of the showers of everlasting mercy, and entered into the life of faith—the heavenly and everlasting life. But he that turned away from that cup was condemned to eternal death. By the terms “life” and “death,” spoken of in the scriptures, is intended the life of faith and the death of unbelief. The generality of the people, owing to their failure to grasp the meaning of these words, rejected and despised the person of the <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="manifestation" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Manifestation">Manifestation</span>, deprived themselves of the light of His divine guidance, and refused to follow the example of that immortal Beauty.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 120" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 120…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="125"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p125" title="Paragraph 125 in the full text">125</a></div><div class="note-text">Such things have come to pass in the days of every <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="manifestation" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Manifestation">Manifestation</span> of God. Even as Jesus said: “Ye must be born again.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="86" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 86">86</sup> Again He saith: “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="87" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 87">87</sup> The purport of these words is that whosoever in every dispensation is born of the Spirit and is quickened by the breath of the Manifestation of Holiness, he verily is of those that have attained unto “life” and “resurrection” and have entered into the “<span class="gl-ref" data-gl="paradise" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: paradise">paradise</span>” of the love of God. And whosoever is not of them, is condemned to “death” and “deprivation,” to the “fire” of unbelief, and to the “wrath” of God. In all the scriptures, the books and chronicles, the sentence of death, of fire, of blindness, of want of understanding and hearing, hath been pronounced against those whose lips have tasted not the ethereal cup of true knowledge, and whose hearts have been deprived of the grace of the holy Spirit in their day. Even as it hath been previously recorded: “Hearts have they with which they understand not.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="88" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 88">88</sup></div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 125" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 125…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
1. What is the Day of Judgment, or the Day of Resurrection, according to Bahá'u'lláh? If the Day of Judgment has already come, in what way was humanity brought to a reckoning with God? (Paragraphs [120](../read.qmd#p120) and [121](../read.qmd#p121))
2. What do "life" and "death" mean according to Bahá'u'lláh? Is eternal life something we can attain only in the next world, or can it begin in this one? (Paragraphs [125](../read.qmd#p125) and [128](../read.qmd#p128))
3. In the Hidden Words Bahá'u'lláh writes:

    > O Son of Being! Bring thyself to account each day ere thou art summoned to a reckoning; for death, unheralded, shall come upon thee and thou shalt be called to give account for thy deeds.
    >
    > [Bahá'u'lláh, *The Hidden Words*, Arabic 31]{.attrib}

    Bahá'ís usually explain this passage in terms of a reckoning that takes place after the death of the physical body. Can it be understood differently? In light of what Bahá'u'lláh has explained, what could the terms "reckoning" and "death" mean in the context of this statement? It may help to note that this statement comes from the Hidden Words which, like the Kitáb-i-Íqán, was revealed during the Baghdad period, before Bahá'u'lláh's declaration.
:::

## Attainment unto the Presence of God {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="149"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p149" title="Paragraph 149 in the full text">149</a></div><div class="note-text">Some have contended that by “attainment unto the Divine Presence” is meant the “Revelation” of God in the Day of Resurrection. Should they assert that the “Revelation” of God signifieth a “Universal Revelation,” it is clear and evident that such revelation already existeth in all things.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 149" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 149…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="150"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p150" title="Paragraph 150 in the full text">150</a></div><div class="note-text">And were they to maintain that by “divine Presence” is meant the “Specific Revelation of God,” expressed by certain <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="sufis" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Ṣúfís">Ṣúfís</span> as the “Most Holy Outpouring,” if this be in the Essence Itself, it is evident that it hath been eternally in the divine Knowledge. Assuming the truth of this hypothesis, “attainment unto the divine Presence” is in this sense obviously possible to no one, inasmuch as this revelation is confined to the innermost Essence, unto which no man can attain.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 150" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 150…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="151"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p151" title="Paragraph 151 in the full text">151</a></div><div class="note-text">And were they to say that by “divine Presence” is meant the “Secondary Revelation of God,” interpreted as the “Holy Outpouring,” this is admittedly applicable to the world of creation, that is, in the realm of the primal and original <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="manifestation" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: manifestation">manifestation</span> of God. Such revelation is confined to His Prophets and chosen Ones, inasmuch as none mightier than they hath come to exist in the world of being. This truth all recognize, and bear witness thereto. These Prophets and chosen Ones of God are the recipients and revealers of all the unchangeable attributes and names of God. They are the mirrors that truly and faithfully reflect the light of God. Whatsoever is applicable to them is in reality applicable to God, Himself, Who is both the Visible and the Invisible. The knowledge of Him, Who is the Origin of all things, and attainment unto Him, are impossible save through knowledge of, and attainment unto, these luminous Beings who proceed from the Sun of Truth. By attaining, therefore, to the presence of these holy Luminaries, the “Presence of God” Himself is attained. From their knowledge, the knowledge of God is revealed, and from the light of their countenance, the splendor of the Face of God is made manifest. Through the manifold attributes of these Essences of Detachment, Who are both the first and the last, the seen and the hidden, it is made evident that He Who is the Sun of Truth is “the First and the Last, the Seen, and the Hidden.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="108" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 108">108</sup> Likewise the other lofty names and exalted attributes of God. Therefore, whosoever, and in whatever Dispensation, hath recognized and attained unto the presence of these glorious, these resplendent and most excellent Luminaries, hath verily attained unto the “Presence of God” Himself, and entered the city of eternal and immortal life. Attainment unto such presence is possible only in the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day of the rise of God Himself through His all-embracing Revelation.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 151" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 151…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
4. Bahá'u'lláh, in these paragraphs, turns to the subject of continuity of Divine Revelation. He says that the idea that "all Revelation is ended", that "the hand of God" is "chained up", and that "the Messengers of God have ceased to be made manifest" is an old one which the Jews initially used to criticize Muḥammad, and that now Muslims are unknowingly voicing the same criticism of the Báb ([¶146](../read.qmd#p146)–[148](../read.qmd#p148)).

    To address this, Bahá'u'lláh calls our attention to the concept of "attaining unto the Presence of God", something which has been "promised unto all people". It is "the highest and most excelling grace bestowed upon men" ([¶148](../read.qmd#p148)), and "no theme hath been more emphatically asserted in the holy scriptures" ([¶149](../read.qmd#p149)). He then considers three hypotheses for what it might mean to attain the presence of God on the Day of Resurrection. Last week we outlined three stages of Divine Revelation: the Essence of God, the Manifestations of God, and the world of creation. Which stage does each hypothesis belong to, and why does Bahá'u'lláh accept or reject each one?

Explore the [References to Attaining the Divine Presence in the Qur'án](../presence.qmd)
:::

## Relation of the Bahá'í Faith to Previous Religions {.passage-heading}

::: {.passage-body}
5. Bahá'u'lláh speaks of Ḥusayn with extraordinary reverence. No warrior on earth was "more excellent and nearer to God... so peerless and incomparable was he", and "there was none to equal or to match him in the world" ([¶135](../read.qmd#p135)). He describes the power of the drops of Ḥusayn's blood ([¶137](../read.qmd#p137)), calls him a "holy soul" who "liveth the life of God" ([¶139](../read.qmd#p139)), and says that these pages could never exhaust the mysteries of his martyrdom ([¶140](../read.qmd#p140)). Clearly Bahá'u'lláh holds Islam in deep respect. At the same time He argues the case for the Cause of the Báb and foreshadows His own Revelation.

    Today there is a tendency among people of all backgrounds, including Bahá'ís, to view their own religion as inherently superior to others. How can we recognize the station and claims of Bahá'u'lláh while avoiding a sense of superiority towards the followers of other Faiths? It may help to consider the words of Shoghi Effendi:

    > Let no one, however, mistake my purpose. The Revelation, of which Bahá'u'lláh is the source and center, abrogates none of the religions that have preceded it, nor does it attempt, in the slightest degree, to distort their features or to belittle their value. It disclaims any intention of dwarfing any of the Prophets of the past, or of whittling down the eternal verity of their teachings. It can, in no wise, conflict with the spirit that animates their claims, nor does it seek to undermine the basis of any man's allegiance to their cause. Its declared, its primary purpose is to enable every adherent of these Faiths to obtain a fuller understanding of the religion with which he stands identified, and to acquire a clearer apprehension of its purpose. It is neither eclectic in the presentation of its truths, nor arrogant in the affirmation of its claims. Its teachings revolve around the fundamental principle that religious truth is not absolute but relative, that Divine Revelation is progressive, not final. Unequivocally and without the least reservation it proclaims all established religions to be divine in origin, identical in their aims, complementary in their functions, continuous in their purpose, indispensable in their value to mankind.
    >
    > [Shoghi Effendi, *The World Order of Bahá'u'lláh*, "The Golden Age of the Cause of Bahá'u'lláh"]{.attrib}
:::
